Questions, answered

Frequently Asked Questions

A few things you might want to know before you begin exploring Virasat.

What is Virasat?
Virasat is a digital space for discovering India's living heritage through food, stories, festivals, games, traditions, objects and regional culture.
Is Virasat free to use?
Yes. The core Virasat experience is designed to be accessible for everyone, with heritage exploration at its heart.
Can I explore heritage by state?
Yes. Visit Explore India to discover living heritage across India's states and union territories.
Can students use Virasat for learning?
Absolutely. Virasat is designed to make learning about culture and heritage interactive, visual and easy to explore.

Heritage is alive when it is remembered, questioned, appreciated and shared.

— Virasat

    Stories that shaped us

    Nani Ki Kahani

    Before there were screens, there were stories. Discover real Indian folk tales with traditional paintings, manuscript art and historical illustrations. Images are representative artworks, not photographs of fictional events.

      VIRASAT / HISTORY

      India was never one straight line.

      Move through urban civilisations, kingdoms, empires, rival courts, battles, trade networks and political turning points that shaped the subcontinent across thousands of years.

      01 · TIMELINE02 · KINGDOMS03 · RIVALRIES04 · COMPARE
      2600 BCE320 CE1526 CE1947 CE
      इतिहास
      02 / CHRONOLOGY

      Follow the timeline.

      Filter by era and see how political centres, trade routes, languages, belief systems and military power shifted over time.

      03 / GREAT POLITIES

      Kingdoms that changed the map.

      A quick lens on major states from different regions and centuries. No single dynasty represents all of Indian history.

      04 / RIVALRIES

      When rulers collided.

      Wars were not isolated spectacles. They shifted capitals, alliances, tax systems, frontiers and the balance of power. These cards focus on what changed, not battlefield gore.

      05 / COMPARE

      Put two powers side by side.

      Compare periods, rulers and legacies. Then explore who might have had the advantage in a hypothetical encounter, and why.

      VS
      Historical periods overlap, borders changed constantly, and dates for early eras can be approximate. This page is an educational overview, not a claim that the subcontinent followed one single political story.

      Ancient Translator

      Brahmi Left-to-right Unicode output

      Note: This is a phonetic script transliterator, not a historical-language grammar translator. Brahmi and Kharosthi are shown simultaneously so there is no script-switching navigation. Unsupported sounds remain visible rather than being silently removed.
